{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Distribution is right-skewed (mean=2.81, sd=2.08, max=201.4) with extreme outliers; consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1); plain ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression or Cochran-Armitage test with paradigm as ordered factor, or chi-square test of independence followed by pairwise proportions tests with multiple comparison correction.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm; severe right skew (mean=0.47, sd=0.47, max=29.8) suggests log-transformation or nonparametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis).",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm; moderate right skew (max=75.4) but may tolerate standard ANOVA; verify homogeneity of variance.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm; bounded [0,1] with mean=0.38, sd=0.24; check distribution for floor/ceiling effects."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Rows are trials from 8 mice; potential clustering by mouse violates independence. Mixed-effects models with random intercept for Mouse are strongly preferred over standard ANOVA.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals; for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed, expect heavy right tails requiring transformation or robust methods.",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test across paradigms; unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) reduces power for smaller groups and increases variance sensitivity.",
    "For Success: Check separation (zero cells) in contingency table; verify adequate counts per paradigm for reliable logistic estimates."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant (or robust equivalent): Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for equal variance, Games-Howell for unequal variance, or Dunn's test for Kruskal-Wallis.",
    "Effect sizes: Partial eta-squared for ANOVA, odds ratios for Success logistic model, or rank-biserial correlation for nonparametric tests.",
    "Focus contrasts: Combined vs single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all stimulated vs Sham to assess additive/multisensory integration effects.",
    "Multiple comparison control: Bonferroni or FDR adjustment for 10 pairwise comparisons across paradigms."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Path Efficiency based on typical multisensory integration benefits, though this is speculative without access to group means.",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance (longer times, lower success, higher AD indicating less directed movement).",
    "Dim vs Bright Visual Only may differ due to visibility constraints, with Bright Visual Only potentially intermediate between Dim and Combined.",
    "ICMS Only as unimodal stimulation may approximate Combined performance if intracortical microstimulation provides strong directional cue.",
    "Success rates near 73% overall suggest ceiling effects unlikely, but paradigm-specific rates may reveal differential effectiveness."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "No access to raw data or group-level means prevents calculation of actual effect sizes and precludes definitive model selection.",
    "Severe imbalance in paradigm sizes (Combined 63.7% of data vs Sham 4.6%) reduces statistical power for Sham comparisons and complicates variance estimation.",
    "Mouse as clustering factor is unmodeled in standard ANOVA; 8 mice with varying trial counts (7233-10986) introduce pseudo-replication and inflated Type I error without mixed-effects framework.",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (max 201s) and Path Efficiency (max 29.8) may disproportionately influence parametric estimates; robust methods needed.",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure; potential confounds from practice or fatigue.",
    "AD interpretation as angular dispersion assumes circular statistics appropriate; standard ANOVA on bounded [0,1] variable may be suboptimal."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD; use generalized linear mixed model (binomial/logit) for Success. Apply Box-Cox or log transformation for right-skewed continuous variables. Report marginal means with 95% CI and pairwise comparisons with Tukey adjustment. If mixed models fail to converge, proceed with robust ANOVA (Welch's) and permutation-based post-hoc tests, acknowledging limitations from unmodeled clustering."
}
